cgroup_hierarchy.mapping_evidence: Mount root /.. exposes a parent above self cgroup namespace root. Self PID is absent from parent cgroup.procs and present in init/cgroup.procs. The self child has no descendant cgroups.

memory.host_vs_cgroup: Host MemAvailable is not the task allowance or the cgroup budget. Cgroup memory includes this workload plus sibling/cache/kernel charges and is dynamic.
memory.task_vs_cgroup: Approved8e9B is total task RSS plus all task-owned tmpfs, including retained old task outputs. It is not an extra8GB allocation on top of current task use, and it is not8GiB.
memory.cache_accounting: memory.stat shmem is included in file, so file+shmem would double-count. Not all file cache is necessarily free/reclaimable; tmpfs output preservation must remain.
memory.allocation_guarantee: Visible hard headroom exceeded8e9B at this snapshot, but this does not reserve that space or prove a future allocation will succeed. Retain live task and cgroup monitoring.

Java_solver_threading.status: Current COCG matrix-vector, dot, preconditioner and vector updates use ordinary sequential Java loops; source basis RHS are also iterated sequentially.
Java_solver_threading.claim_boundary: A4CPU policy or JVM ActiveProcessorCount=4 does not parallelize these loops or establish4x speedup. JVM GC/JIT can use helper threads without making the numerical solver parallel.
Java_solver_threading.BLAS_boundary: NumPy/OpenBLAS presence does not accelerate the plain Java solver. BLAS thread control applies only to operations actually using that BLAS library; NumPy elementwise/broadcast operations need not use BLAS.
Java_solver_threading.future_parallelism: Any explicit numerical parallelization needs a declared implementation and validation. Independent duplicate owners/workers are not authorized by raising the CPU cap.

conclusion: The visible environment supports an upper bound of4 sustained CPU equivalents and16GiB cgroup memory, with roughly8.7GB instantaneous hard headroom observed. The approved total task envelope8e9B is below that hard limit, while existing task tmpfs/RSS must remain included and runtime monitoring is still required. Existing solver numerical loops are serial.
